subject: Private Host: Forensics window and one-time credit request
messages:
From: Cara Lin <cara.lin@helios.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helios.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private hosting - forensics access & credit ask

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're excited to proceed with the private VPC deployment but have one remaining gating item from our security team: a timeboxed forensics/incident evidence window where Helios' retained third-party forensics vendor can access a narrow slice of logs and ephemeral host artifacts for post-incident investigation.

Request details:
- Scope: read-only access to application logs (S3), VPC flow logs, and a short snapshot of ephemeral host memory/disk limited to the suspected instance only. No host-level credentials or SSH.
- Window: one continuous 72-hour window (customer-initiated) within the first 12 months of production; customer pays for forensic vendor costs.
- Control: access to be mediated by Redwood engineers through a supervised remote session; access audit captured in our logs.
- Data handling: Helios will sign a narrow addendum limiting use to incident forensics and prohibiting retention beyond 30 days.

Helios acknowledges the operational risk and is willing to accept a stronger indemnity carveout for this access. To make this feasible commercially, they are asking Redwood to provide a one-time credit against year-one committed fees (proposed $25,000) in exchange for granting this limited variance.

Attaching their forensics_request_form.pdf and a short security synopsis.

Can you advise what level of concession we can offer and whether this requires executive sign-off? We'd like to avoid losing momentum on the SOW.

Thanks,
Cara Lin
Head of Security Programs
Helios Therapeutics

Attachments: forensics_request_form.pdf, redwood-security-snapshot.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Private hosting - forensics access & credit ask

Team — forwarding Helios' request. Key asks: 72-hour, customer-initiated forensics window with supervised access and a one-time $25k credit request.

My read: security is comfortable with a supervised, audited session if Legal signs a very tight addendum and Engineering can implement a short-lived snapshot flow (no SSH, no long-term host access). The main questions for Deal Desk / Finance: are we able to offer a one-time commercial concession for a private hosting variance like this? Also need clarity on SLA exposure and whether we can lock this under a SOW amendment with conditions (no egress except the supervised snapshot we mediate).

Can you weigh in with proposed concession and any non-negotiable guardrails? I can draft the SOW language once we decide.

Tessa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private hosting - forensics access & credit ask

Tessa — thanks for flagging. I've reviewed the forensics_request_form and redwood-security-snapshot. Security and Eng side notes: the supervised snapshot flow is implementable but it is a non-trivial ops lift for a private deployment (we need runbook changes and a guarded engineer remote session).

Commercially, I don't want to set a $25k precedent unless Execs approve. Proposed compromise: offer a one-time credit of $15,000 (applied to year-one committed fees) and require Helios to sign our tight forensics addendum + an SOC attestation before granting the window. Conditions to include in SOW amendment:
- Forensics window limited to 72 hours, single occurrence in 12 months
- Redwood-led snapshot process; Helios' vendor only observes via audited remote session
- No host-level key issuance; no retention beyond 30 days
- Customer pays for vendor costs and any extra ops overtime

Risk note: this still elevates operational complexity and slightly increases failure modes during the snapshot. Recommend we require approval from SVP Sales or Head of Product for the final credit.

If Kimberly is aligned, I can log this as a Deal Desk exception and prepare the amendment language + HubSpot note.

Ben Carter
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private hosting - forensics access & credit ask

Thanks for the summary and proposed guardrails. I approve moving forward under the following executive-cleared terms:

1) One-time credit: $15,000 applied to year-one committed fees (non-recurring). This must be recorded on the quote and visible to Finance.
2) Forensics window: single 72-hour window within 12 months, customer-initiated. Access only via Redwood-supervised remote session; no host credentials.
3) Legal: mandatory forensics addendum signed by customer with explicit data-use and retention limits (30 days max).
4) Ops/Eng: we require a pre-scheduled runbook and a Redwood engineer on-call; customer will reimburse any overtime beyond normal support hours.
5) Compliance: SOC attestation or equivalent required before we enable the window.

I am signing off on the $15k credit pending SVP Sales acknowledgement — Ben, please route to SVP for FYI and request formal OK in the Deal Desk ticket. Tessa, please respond to Cara with the approved terms and attach the forensics addendum draft. Also add the amendment and the DocuSign link to HubSpot under deal DEAL-HELIOS-2026-11.

Kimberly Park
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
